title: US floated NATO membership for Ukraine in return for leaving Donbas, Zelensky says
dek: Ukraine's president said it was the first time Washington had linked territory to NATO entry. He refused to cede land Russia does not hold, but said he would put any full package to a national vote.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
US negotiators asked Ukraine whether it would withdraw from the eastern Donbas region if it were allowed to join NATO, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday, the first time, he said, that territorial concessions had been tied to membership of the Western military alliance.

"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?'" Mr Zelensky said, according to reports. He said he would not give up territory, and that the areas in question were ones Russia does not control. Neither the White House, the US State Department, NATO nor the Kremlin had publicly responded to his account by Sunday afternoon India time.

## What Zelensky said

Mr Zelensky said the question showed that "NATO is back on the agenda". He set out conditions: if Ukraine received a full package from the United States and NATO partners, including security guarantees, military and reconstruction funding and a recovery plan, "then I will ask our Ukrainian society what it thinks", putting any arrangement over Donbas to a national referendum. Any deal, he said, would not recognise occupied land as Russian.

He ruled out neutrality, which Moscow has demanded, saying it would require changing Ukraine's constitution. "If Putin expects Ukraine's neutrality to be enshrined, that's not going to happen," he said. He also said Kyiv was negotiating "specific" Western guarantees, and that "Putin's desire to change borders in Europe is a fact."

## Background

The remarks followed the latest rounds of talks in Abu Dhabi, which produced a large prisoner exchange this week but no breakthrough on ending the war. US envoys then travelled to Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin. At a summit in Ireland, European Union leaders agreed that Europe's team for any peace talks would include Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and EU officials, and would talk to US and Ukrainian officials but not to Russia.

Russia has long called Ukrainian membership of NATO a red line, and cited it as one reason for its full-scale invasion in February 2022. It demands that Ukraine withdraw from the parts of Donbas it still holds. Mr Zelensky has said Donbas is "not real estate".

The fighting has continued alongside the diplomacy. Russian officials said on Friday that about 1,200 Ukrainian drones had been launched at Russia in a day, with oil infrastructure among the targets. Ukraine reported Russian attacks on a hospital and on the port of Odesa, and an air attack damaged a residential building in Zaporizhzhia. None of these figures could be independently verified.

## Why it matters for India

India has consistently called for dialogue and diplomacy to end the war, and keeps close ties with both Moscow and Western capitals. Any settlement that redraws Europe's security map would shape India's ties with both Moscow and the West, and would matter for oil prices and for India's long-standing defence supplies from Russia.

## What happens next

Mr Putin, Mr Trump and China's President Xi Jinping are due to hold their first three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen next week, where Ukraine is expected to be discussed. Any US or Russian response to Mr Zelensky's account would be the next sign of whether the idea is being pursued.
